title: ReCG: ReRAM-Accelerated Sparse Conjugate Gradient
problem: Sparse Conjugate Gradient solvers implemented on storage-compute separated architectures suffer from poor performance due to irregular memory access patterns and large data transmission overhead between memory and compute units.
motivation: Sparse linear systems are fundamental to scientific computing, and accelerating their solution improves overall performance of HPC applications.
method: The design leverages ReRAM (resistive memory) as a compute-in-memory fabric to co-locate data and computation, eliminating the traditional storage-compute bottleneck. By performing sparse matrix-vector multiplication and CG kernel operations directly in ReRAM, the approach reduces expensive data movements. The architecture handles irregular memory access patterns inherent to sparse operations through ReRAM's flexible in-memory computation model.
key_novelty: Using ReRAM compute-in-memory technology to directly accelerate sparse conjugate gradient solvers and eliminate storage-compute separation bottlenecks.
contributions: ReRAM-based accelerator architecture optimized for sparse CG workloads
Techniques for handling irregular memory access patterns in sparse kernels
Demonstration of reduced data transmission through near-data processing
